You can do this but it's not recommended at all and not even the quickest or best way to go about what you want to achieve. .

Simply do this. Copy the ENTIRE contents of your home folder somewhere, making sure any important personal files are intact and not damaged. Reinstall 15.10 with a fresh install USB/DVD ISO, then paste back your home folder, when it asks to overwrite, do so. I have done this countless times even across different distros and never had an issue. You will have to reinstall any software, for example VLC, but all of your settings for that software should be saved in your home folder config files meaning you wont have to tweak settings again in each program.

Note; if you want to future proof yourself from having to do this you can install manually and set up a separate home folder partition that will carry across any upgrades or reinstalls but it's not necessary to do either. My method works the same.

Better yet, put the home folder contents into a partition, reinstall setting that partition as /home.

No external equipment needed and it's will be even easier to do next time and he can even duel boot linux distros.
